title: Co-ownership disputes - partition vs sale by mutual consent
p1:
Two people can own the same property and still disagree on what happens next.

But many assume the only solution is to sell immediately. That is not always true.
p2:
A common misunderstanding is that every co-owner has to accept a sale. In reality, a co-owner may seek partition, which means dividing the ownership or property interest so each person can move forward separately.

A surprising point: a property does not always have to be physically split. Courts may consider practical ways to separate interests when a physical division is not possible.
p3:
If all co-owners agree, a sale by mutual consent is often faster and gives everyone more control over the process, price, and timing.

When agreement is impossible, partition becomes a legal route to resolve the deadlock. The best option depends on the property, the relationship between owners, and whether cooperation is possible.

Knowing the difference can prevent years of unnecessary disputes.
conclusion: If co-owners cannot agree on keeping a property, would you prefer a legal partition process or a mutually agreed sale? What factors would influence your choice?
